source.title: The Longest Verse
source.summary: Ayat al-Dayn: the Quran's most detailed verse is about debt. What does that tell us?
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: Verse 2:282 of the Quran, known as Ayat al-Dayn, is the longest single verse in the entire scripture. Not a verse about prayer, pilgrimage, or fasting, but about how to write a debt contract. It mandates written documentation, witnesses, and the protection of both creditor and debtor. Scholars have marveled at this for centuries: why would God dedicate the most detailed verse in His final revelation to commercial transactions? This episode unpacks Ayat al-Dayn word by word, explores what classical scholars like al-Jassas and al-Qurtubi said about its implications, and argues that Islam treats financial justice not as a footnote to faith but as its foundation.
